Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `236904f8d8736ced865f6d4745a122388a26feba`

Reviewed the head whole (no earlier contract review on this PR). Inputs: card #12413 (body, triage `6183369572`, claim `6183679413`, dev report `6183934105`), PR #12420 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at merge-base `4b0a087a6`: 4 files, +191/−10), the check-runs on the head, and the spec row `ListDraftsResponseSchema.drafts[]` read from `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` at the `@objectstack/spec@18.0.0-next.1` tag (`84073bf6e`; the row is byte-identical to the local objectstack checkout at `18.0.0-next.0`). The head's lockfile resolves `@objectstack/spec` to `18.0.0-next.1` for `data-objectstack`, so the type the published declaration derives from is the one read here.

### ① Derived judgments

Spec row at `18.0.0-next.1`: `type: string`, `name: string`, `member?: string` (`z.string().optional()`), `label: I18nLabel | null` (required, nullable), `packageId: string | null`, `updatedAt: string | null`, `updatedBy: string | null`. `ListDraftsResponse` is `z.input` of the schema; the row has no default or transform, so the input and parsed faces agree.

1. **`MetadataDraftHeader` is derived from the spec row — right.** `export interface MetadataDraftHeader extends Pick<ListDraftsRow, 'type' | 'name' | 'packageId' | 'updatedAt' | 'updatedBy'> { member?: ListDraftsRow['member'] }` with `type ListDraftsRow = ListDraftsResponse['drafts'][number]`. The five pre-existing keys now come from the spec symbol and their types are unchanged (`string`, `string`, `string | null` ×3 — the spec declares exactly those; the new `.types.test.ts` pins each by type equality and pins `keyof` to exactly the six keys). Nothing removed, nothing retyped: the only widening is `member?: string | undefined`. This is the triage ruling ("derive the type from the spec's row type rather than adding a hand-copied key") met as written.
2. **`member` declared in the interface body rather than in the `Pick` — right.** It is still typed from the spec (`ListDraftsRow['member']`, pinned equal to `SpecDraftRow['member']`), keeps the optional modifier, and avoids the `no-empty-object-type` lint on an empty extending body. Nit, not a surface fault: the changeset prose says "`Pick` over `type`, `name`, `member`, …" — written at `fd19458d9`, before the body reshape at `236904f8d` — while the code picks five and declares `member`. The published type is the same either way.
3. **Leaving out the spec row's required `label` — right for this card.** The card asks for `member`; `label` is a second key, declared REQUIRED (nullable) on the spec row, and picking it would have the client assert a server vintage it cannot verify (the same reason `MetadataPublishPackageDraftsResult` is `Partial`). A `Pick` that omits a key is a narrower face of the same row, not a contradiction of it. The omission is declared in the type's docblock, the PR's Acceptance notes and the dev report; see ③ for the follow-up.
4. **`MetadataSaveAdvisoryEvent.member` is additive and set only when non-empty — right.** One optional key, typed `MetadataDraftHeader['member']`; the single emit in `publishDraft` spreads `...(options.member ? { member: options.member } : {})`, the same truthiness rule as the `?member=` query parameter two dozen lines above. The other three emits (`publish`, `save`, the batch door) are untouched in the diff. The pin covers `undefined`, `{}` and `{ member: '' }` (key absent) and `{ member: 'zh-CN' }` (key present).
5. **Hook cast removal is behaviour-neutral — right.** `useMetadataClient()` returns `MetadataClient`, so `client.listDrafts?.({})` already resolved to `Promise<MetadataDraftHeader[]>`; the `as any[]` was the only thing hiding the row type. The runtime expression (`|| []`, the `filter` on `type`/`name`, the `typeof d.member === 'string' && d.member` guard) is unchanged; `d.member as string` → `d.member` is a no-op after the guard. No URL or payload moves.
6. **Interface kind — the premise in the dispatch brief does not hold, and the change is compatible.** `MetadataDraftHeader` was `export interface` on `main` and is `export interface` on the head; the dev report says "now an interface extending Pick", not "changed from a type alias", and the PR body says "Shape kind kept". For consumers: declaration merging and `implements` keep working, an interface extending a `Pick` is structurally what the hand-written body was for the five keys, object literals typed as the header still type-check, and an added optional property breaks no reader. The import `ListDraftsResponse` from `@objectstack/spec/api` is type-only, against a package already declared in `dependencies` (`^18.0.0-next.1`), and `Test (dist pins)` is green on the head, so the published `dist/index.d.ts` resolves it.
7. **No other public-surface change.** `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts` already re-exports `MetadataDraftHeader` and `MetadataSaveAdvisoryEvent`; `ListDraftsRow` is a module-private alias; `listDrafts()`'s signature and `draftLedgerMayHold`'s read are untouched.

Check-runs on `236904f8d` at the time of this record: 19 completed `success` (`Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Lint`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Test (shard 4/16, 5/16, 7/16, 9/16, 12/16)`, the five `Changeset *` gates, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Live E2E (informational)`, `label`), 3 `skipped` (coverage, dependabot), none failed. Still `in_progress` when read, so NOT claimed by this record: `Type Check`, `Repo Gates`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, and test shards 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16 of 16. The type-level pins in ①.1–①.6 are therefore read off the diff and the dev's reported `tsc` runs, and the still-running `Type Check` run on the head is the gate that confirms them before the queue.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/12413-draft-header-member.md` declares `@object-ui/data-objectstack: minor` and `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`. That matches what the diff publishes: two published types widened additively (a minor; objectui never declares `major`), and one shipped app-shell file changed with no behaviour change (a patch). Both packages sit in the changeset `fixed` group, so the group bumps together either way; the declaration is still the honest one. `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check` and `Changeset Claim Re-read` are all green on the head. The PR's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line matches the claim's and triage's reading, and matches the diff: nothing is removed or narrowed. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`usePendingDrafts.ts` untouched (premise correction) — answered, correct.** On the head the file does its own `fetch` of `_drafts`, types the rows as `Array<Record<string, unknown>>`, and declares its own `member?: string` on `PendingDraft`; its `as string` follows a `typeof` check on `unknown`. It never reads `MetadataClient.listDrafts()` or `MetadataDraftHeader`, so this widening cannot reach it, and leaving it alone is the right scope. Its pins stay in the full-suite run the dev reports and in the CI test shards.
- **`label` still omitted; a draft-only Studio rail entry may show a machine name (read-only inference, carrier: none) — answered and escalated.** The omission is right for this card (①.3). The rail question is a separate card: whether `MetadataDraftHeader` should pick `label` (a second widening, and a vintage question the lane has to rule on) and whether `loadPackageSurfaces` / `mergeSurfaces` in `packageSurfaces.ts` should read it. Not a FAIL condition here; it is a follow-up for `domain:ui` to file with the dev's dedupe words (`draft-only label machine name; listDrafts label; packageSurfaces draft label`). This review posts one comment and does not file it.
- **`publishPackageDrafts` per-element advisory events carry no `member` — answered, correct.** The spec's `PublishPackageDraftsResponseSchema.published[]` element at `18.0.0-next.1` declares `type`, `name`, `version`, `advisories`; no `member`. Nothing to carry.
- **`open_questions`: none** in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
